newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian stocks jump, but AMS slumps.
newsitem.headline: Austrian stocks jump, but AMS slumps.

text.p: Austrian shares went into a long weekend on a buoyant note on Thursday, but chip-maker AMS fell six percent after disappointing nine-month earnings.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips gained 6.77 points, or 0.64 percent, to close at 1,067.07 after earlier slipping to 1,055.25.
Traders said the rebound was above all fuelled by demand for VA Stahl and VA Tech stock and expect the market to trade with a solid tone next week.
"It also depends on the U.S. elections, whether the Americans then significantly raise interest rates -- but I don't think that'll happen," said a trader.
Traders sooner expect the ATX to head for 1,080 points next week, pointing out that 1,060 has offered firm support.
Of the ATX's constituents, 16 advanced, four fell and one was unchanged. The market will be closed on Friday due to All Saints holiday.
The day's best performing blue chip was Mayr Melnhof, adding on 2.17 percent to 523 schillings.
AMS was the worst, falling 5.95 percent to 678 after its earnings continued to disappoint investors. AMS' nine-month pre-tax profit slumped 32.7 percent to 148 million schillings.
Traders said the share price could fall further to its old lows of 640/650 schillings.
The all-share Vienna bourse index advanced 2.21 points, or 0.54 percent, to 410.47.
The November ATX future gained four points to 1,065 on turnover of 1,042 contracts. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 253
